answer.rationale: P99 latency spiking 5x target 2 hours after release during peak settlement traffic signals a regression in the recent build. Memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback of a problematic release cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact, and memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions early. The timing (release → latency climb) and the write-path focus during settlement peak suggests the new code is the vector. Rollback is the fastest path to stability without sacrificing capacity or introducing additional complexity during peak load. This preserves the option to investigate root cause post-recovery while restoring service to target latency immediately. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) would degrade customer experience by failing requests; capacity addition takes time we don't have; failover and read replica routing don't address a write-path regression.
